definitions.gloss: a Japanese leafy green vegetable in the mustard family (Brassica rapa var. nipposinica) with slender white stems and deeply notched, jagged green leaves, eaten both raw and cooked; mizuna, potherb mustard
definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese leafy vegetable originally cultivated in Kyoto and considered one of the classic Kyoto vegetables ({京野菜|きょうやさい}). It has a mild, slightly peppery flavor and a crisp, watery texture. Traditionally eaten cooked in hot pot dishes such as はりはり{鍋|なべ}, it is now extremely common raw in salads, where the jagged leaves add crunch. In recent decades mizuna has spread worldwide and is popular in Western salad mixes under the name 'mizuna.'

notes:
Written {水菜|みずな} with ⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧ (water) + {菜|な} (leafy vegetable). The name refers to the traditional cultivation method of growing the plant in channels of flowing water, without fertilizer — hence 'water vegetable.'

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {水菜|みずな}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦サラダ→サラダ：01364_sarada⟧: mizuna salad
- {水菜|みずな}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{豚肉|ぶたにく}→豚肉：02956_butaniku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{鍋|なべ}→鍋：01038_nabe⟧: pork and mizuna hot pot
- {水菜|みずな}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{洗|あら}う→洗う：00827_arau⟧: to wash mizuna
- {水菜|みずな}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{刻|きざ}む→刻む：03918_kizamu⟧: to chop mizuna
- シャキシャキ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{水菜|みずな}: crisp mizuna

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {京菜|きょうな}: an older name for the same plant, emphasizing its Kyoto origin; still seen on traditional product labels.
- {壬生菜|みぶな}: mibuna — a very close relative with rounded rather than jagged leaves, also from Kyoto.
- ⟦{小松菜|こまつな}→小松菜：12520_komatsuna⟧: komatsuna, Japanese mustard spinach — a sturdier green with broad, smooth leaves; mild and slightly sweet.
- ⟦ほうれん{草|そう}→ほうれん草：05188_hourensou⟧: spinach — softer leaves and deeper green; cooked rather than raw in Japanese cuisine.
- ⟦チンゲン{菜|さい}→チンゲン菜：16115_chingensai⟧: bok choy — a Chinese leafy vegetable with thick white stems.

CULINARY USES:
- はりはり⟦{鍋|なべ}→鍋：01038_nabe⟧: a traditional Kansai hot pot of whale or pork with large quantities of mizuna.
- Added raw to green salads for crunch.
- Quickly parboiled (⟦お{浸|ひた}し→お浸し：10245_ohitashi⟧-style) with a light soy sauce dressing.
- Stir-fried with other vegetables.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Mizuna is classified as one of the {京野菜|きょうやさい} (Kyoto vegetables), a prestigious group of traditional vegetables associated with Kyoto cuisine. It is available in supermarkets year-round today, but its peak season is winter.
